evidence: Cic. Phil. 2.76: redīre lūce, nōn tenebrīs (Lewis & Short s.v. tenebrae)
terms.comment: The ablative alone: in the dark, under cover of night. Traupman 86 gives dē nocte for “in the dark”; that is “in the course of the night” (see night).

sources: Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
